stem.text: Water flows into a pond from a stream at a rate modeled by \( E(t) = \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{4} \right)} + 4 \) cubic meters per hour and drains out of it at a rate modeled by \( L(t) = 3 \cos{\left(\frac{t}{2} \right)} + 2 \) cubic meters per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 2 \), where t is measured in hours. At time t = 0 the pond holds 20 cubic meters. Using a calculator, find the amount in the pond at time t = 2. Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The net rate is inflow minus outflow, \( E(t) - L(t) \), so the answer is \( 20 + \int_{0}^{2} \left(E(t) - L(t)\right)\,dt \).
worked_solution.rule_named: net rate as inflow minus outflow

worked_solution.text: With a calculator in radian mode, \( \int_{0}^{2} \left(E(t) - L(t)\right)\,dt \) is approximately -0.428 (more places are kept).
Adding the initial amount gives about 19.572 cubic meters.

options.derivation: the inflow and outflow rates added instead of subtracted
L(t) substituted without parentheses, so only its constant term is subtracted and its cosine term is added
the integral of the net rate reported as the amount, with the initial 20 cubic meters left out
